newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds modest gains late with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds modest gains late with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held slim gains late Thursday in moderate activity, with reports of firmer physical prices and a bullish inventory report Wednesday still underpinning the complex, sources said.
At 1410 EDT, August was still up by 1.7 cents at $2.165 per million British thermal units, while September 1.2 cents higher at $2.105. Most others were steady to 1.2 cents higher.

"I think we saw some follow through today from the stats (AGA data) last night, but I'm surprised we're still up," said one Texas-based trader, noting gas production cut by Hurricane Danny was back and Midwest and Northeast temperatures this week were fairly cool.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 58 bcf, well below average estimates in the 75-80 bcf range.
Traders said injection programs were slowed last week by record heat and weather-related production cuts, a factor propping the cash this week as buyers step up the pace of stock building.
"People lost some supply last week because of the hurricane and they need to make up that gas before the end of the month," a Houston trader said.
But few expected the impact to last, with more seasonal temperatures forecast to return to the Midwest and East next week after a brief warm up over the weekend.

Chart traders agreed August was range bound, but some said the wide spread between cash and futures, now about eight cents in favor of the physical market, made it hard to be an aggressive bear with only three days before the spot month goes off the board on Tuesday. Cash and paper often converge just ahead of expiration.

August support was seen at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week was in the $2.21 area, with further resistance pegged at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.
In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices firmed four cents to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up about a nickel to the mid-teens. New York city gate gas firmed a few cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
NYMEX said 26,905 contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, August climbed three cents to $2.095, while deferreds were still steady to 1.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 7.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
